title: Family Truth Reconciliation — the standing rules, and the JVM/web remainder
purpose: M14, M37 and M49 each certify the JVM and Web families as done, while 14 M49-CONV issues remain open across every family. The mechanism is scope: each milestone measured its own artifact (M14 the analyzer oracle, M37 the families against each other, M49 external claims against code) and none measured payload truth across the seam emit -> store -> query -> tool, so every new dimension looked like a new phase instead of an unfinished one. M60 closes the remainder, converts 'family closed' from prose into a computed boolean (green gate AND zero non-alive payload cells), and establishes the standing rules that bind every milestone so no new milestone is minted to carry work that belongs to an existing one. Fold target: M49. Hand-off: M14-clean receives one milestone for all remaining analyzers.
invariant: A family may be called closed only when its closure gate is green AND every payload cell of every onboarded language in it is alive — produced by the analyzer, preserved by the store, reachable at query, and truthful at the tool. Any closure claim not backed by a live gate is itself a defect. No new milestone may be created to carry work that belongs to an existing one.

standingRules.rule: No new milestone for work that belongs to an existing one; findings become issues under existing milestones.
A family is closed only when its closure gate is green AND its payload matrix has zero non-alive cells.
Every finding document must be registered as an issue before it is worked. A doc is not a queue.
Fold contract: at close, M60's family results are recorded into M49 as the evidence its jvm/web closure claims are true.
M14-clean receives one milestone covering all remaining analyzers, each carrying the accumulated checks of every prior milestone.

One line base for every line in the payload: `line_number`, `range`, `decoratorLine` and the `metadata.line` mirror are 1-based, and no analyzer may emit a mirror that is not provably so (#873; the cpp/hpp rows carry no `line_number` at all, so a wrong mirror there was the row's entire line).

No analyzer may NAME something with a placeholder literal. When a fallback has nothing truthful to say the honest state is ABSENCE, not the string "unknown" — a literal in a name-bearing field becomes a symbol (or an edge endpoint) that does not exist in the source (`source: owner || "unknown"` attributes an edge to a symbol named "unknown" that no file contains, and every consumer downstream can then match, count and display it). Enforced by an AST census over every analyzer (script/m60/sentinel-census.ts) against an exact-count, shrink-only register (validation/m60/symbol-sentinel-register.json): a new site, a grown site and a vanished site all fail. Owner standard 2026-09-21 (reviews/m60-oo-family-plan.md §3.7/R2): the OO family reaches zero as lane work with fixtures and mutants; the runtime half — no emitted row carries a placeholder as a name — is disclosed as outstanding in the register rather than implied by a green gate.

No analyzer may publish a framework capability it does not have, or name one framework twice. The family contract is three metadata keys — `framework` (the deterministic primary pick), `detectedFrameworks` (always an array, [] when none), `frameworkPatterns` (aligned) — plus the `hasFrameworkIntelligence` capability claim; the class the rule measures is every way that surface can be published false (dead trigger surface, append-write duplication, name divergence, dominated trigger, unjustified claim, missing contract key). Enforced by a syntactic census over every analyzer (script/m60/framework-surface-census.ts, 17 self-tests) against an exact-count, shrink-only register (validation/m60/framework-surface-register.json) with a recorded OO target so an OO lane's violations cannot be absorbed into the global baseline; the runtime half is script/m60/framework-surface-probe.ts over fixtures and real corpora. Owner standard 2026-09-22 (reviews/m60-oo-family-plan.md §3, C7).

Every analyzer emits the family's declared-type reference graph: a `references` edge from the declaration that WRITES a type name (field, variable declaration, parameter, return type, property, indexer, event, delegate) to the type it names, marked `metadata.relationshipType === "declared_type"` (rust's R13 header names this a family standard, mirrors go/c/zig). The rule exists because an ABSENT capability emits NOTHING: every other gate asks whether an edge that EXISTS is right, so a lane that never emits a whole class of edge reads clean in all of them — csharp's graph was missing while ten sibling lanes had it and survived an entire review wave, recorded in reviews/csharp/master-review.md as a 'recorded gap for its own wave'. Enforced by a runtime census that drives each lane's real analyzer through ASTEngine with a holder-symbol CONTROL, so a snippet the grammar rejects can never read as a missing capability (script/m60/declared-type-refs-census.ts), against a per-lane register (validation/m60/declared-type-register.json): an unregistered lane, a regressed lane, a lane that closes its gap without flipping the register, a lane emitting under a divergent marker, a not-exercised or errored lane, an absent artifact, and OO debt above the recorded target all fail. Measured 2026-09-22: 9 lanes emit it under the family marker, c emits it under `type_reference` (divergent marker, recorded, not convicted), ruby is ruled exempt-dynamic, and 9 lanes emit nothing — five of them OO (csharp, dart, php, swift, objc), the family's largest remaining single axis. Owner standard 2026-09-22.

Every relationship TARGET must be spelled the way the lane spells its own symbols. The differential oracle derives its truth from the same rules the analyzer runs, so a spelling that BOTH sides fabricate identically produces AGREEMENT — and every per-edge gate in the family (the M59.A7 line contract, the depth draws, the fixtures) asks whether an edge that EXISTS is right, so none of them can see it. php's `$o->{'lit'}` published the string literal `'lit'` as a member name, `$o->{2}` an integer, and `include $this->baseDir . 'revision-info.php'` a whole expression as a path — all emitted IDENTICALLY by the oracle, invisible to the differential by construction, and invisible to the line oracle too because the quotes and digits really are written on the claimed line. Enforced by a runtime census (script/m60/target-spelling-census.ts) driving each lane's real analyzer through ASTEngine over a spread draw of LANG_REPOS + SECOND_CORPUS, against a per-lane register (validation/m60/target-spelling-register.json): the CONVICTING classes are `literal` (the whole target is a quoted string or a bare number), `whitespace`, and `delimiter` (`;`, `(`, `)`, `{`, `}`, `,`), none of which any language in the family can declare and none of which needs calibration; the REPORTED class is `separator` (a non-alphanumeric character absent from the lane's own symbol alphabet), recorded and ruled rather than convicted, because qualified names legitimately carry `.`, `:`, `/`, `@`, `$`, `?`, `!`, `-` — 21 of 24 lanes carry one, and the first draft's conviction of that class was refuted by its own measurement. Measured 2026-09-23 at sample 30 per draw: 3 lanes clean (php, rust, zig), 11 carry a provable fabricated spelling (javascript, kotlin, scala, java, groovy, cpp, csharp, dart, swift, haskell, elixir), 9 have separator vocabulary measured and owed, and 2 draws could not adjudicate the separator class at all. The php lane's two defects were fixed in the same round; the rest are recorded per lane with owners, and OO debt above the recorded target fails. Owner standard 2026-09-23.
